name: a replacement beside a null object patch
why: null is not an operation. The exactly-one rule refuses a node that names two THINGS TO DO; "o": null says there is nothing to do, so nothing is discarded by applying the replacement

name: a positional patch beside a null object patch
why: the same, with the surviving operation second in the dispatch order

name: an object patch beside a null keyed patch
why: and again for the keyed field, which is a pointer in Go and an object here

name: a null replacement beside every other field null
why: "r" present and holding null IS an operation -- that distinction is the reason the Go type carries a value rather than a pointer -- while the other three being null are not
